# Launcher and agent command help

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_cli_reference.py. Don't edit by hand. -->

This page is the `--help` text of every `openadapt` and `openadapt agent`
command, from openadapt 1.23.0, openadapt-flow 3.3.0, openadapt-agent 2.2.2. It's generated from each program's parser, and
CI fails when it differs from those versions. [Commands](cli.md) explains
what each command is for, and [All Flow commands](flow-commands.md) lists
the `openadapt flow` commands. The launcher's research commands
(`capture`, `eval`, `serve`, and `train`) aren't listed.

`openadapt agent ...` runs `openadapt-agent ...`; the help text uses the
second name.

## openadapt

### `openadapt`

```text
Usage: openadapt [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Record, compile and run workflows with OpenAdapt.

  Compile a demonstrated workflow into deterministic local replay. Healthy
  runs make no model calls; configured checks can halt on ambiguity. Native
  and remote substrates use platform-specific extras and permissions;
  training/evaluation commands are research.

  Quick Start (Python 3.10-3.12):
      python -m pip install --upgrade openadapt
      openadapt quickstart

  Manual Demo Lifecycle:
      openadapt flow demo-record --out rec
      openadapt compile rec --out bundle --name demo
      openadapt flow lint bundle
      openadapt flow certify bundle --policy permissive
      openadapt flow replay bundle --demo-app

  Lint lists the demo's coverage gaps. The demo has warnings, so `lint
  --strict` exits 1 on it. The manual demo is runnable but not certified for
  consequential work. Use `openadapt flow tutorial` for the effect-verified
  first run.

  Give an MCP client your compiled workflows:
      openadapt agent serve --bundles DIR --mode production

Options:
  --version  Show the version and exit.
  --help     Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  demo      Try the demonstration and tutorial
  verify    Check effects, receipts, and evidence
  record    Record a task and its narration
  teach     Teach a correction to a stopped workflow
  compile   Compile and prepare workflow bundles
  run       Run, resume, and route workflows
  approve   Review and approve paused work
  undo      Declare and run approved undo steps
  qualify   Qualify a workflow for its intended use
  repair    Review, test, and promote repairs
  inspect   Inspect workflows, runs, and reports
  workflow  Manage reusable workflow libraries
  services  Run local services and connectors
  setup     Configure connections, privacy, and access
  research  Run benchmarks and research tools
  wrap      Run an agent task once, then reuse its checked compiled tool

Legacy commands:
  agent       Serve compiled workflows to an MCP client...
  bench       Public benchmarks you can rerun with your...
  capture     Standalone local human GUI capture...
  connect     Connect this computer to the signed-in...
  deploy      Check this host and print the safe...
  doctor      Check system requirements and dependencies.
  eval        Research: evaluate computer-use models on...
  flow        Run the canonical demonstration compiler...
  pull        Download a packaged workflow: `openadapt...
  quickstart  Show a task once, run it, then watch it...
  seal        Check an OpenAdapt Seal offline:...
  serve       Research: serve the training dashboard and...
  shadow      Check each write your agent makes against...
  train       Research: train ML models on captured...
  version     Show version information for all packages.
```

### `openadapt agent`

```text
Usage: openadapt agent [OPTIONS]

  Serve compiled workflows to an MCP client (openadapt-agent).

  Every argument passes to openadapt-agent unchanged. Use this form where only
  `openadapt` is on PATH, as after `uv tool install openadapt` or pipx, which
  keep the `openadapt-agent` executable inside the tool's own environment.
  Nothing is written to stdout before the bridge starts, so an MCP client can
  launch this command directly.

Options:
  --help  Show this message and exit.
```

### `openadapt connect`

```text
Usage: openadapt connect [OPTIONS]

  Connect this computer to the signed-in OpenAdapt Cloud workspace.

  The browser creates a five-minute, one-use pairing. This command claims it
  and saves the resulting workspace credential in the OS keychain. It cannot
  execute arbitrary terminal commands or grant browser access to the shell.

Options:
  --pairing TEXT                  Five-minute pairing code from Cloud settings
  --uri TEXT                      Exact openadapt://connect desktop deep link
  --host TEXT                     Cloud origin (default:
                                  https://app.openadapt.ai)
  --device-name TEXT              Name shown for this computer
  --destination-kind [openadapt-managed|customer-managed|local]
                                  Trust class for the pairing destination
  --trusted-host TEXT             Exact allowed customer-managed origin
                                  (repeatable)
  --help                          Show this message and exit.
```

### `openadapt deploy`

```text
Usage: openadapt deploy [OPTIONS]

  Check this host and print the safe Flow/Desktop deployment path.

  This launcher command does not create another runtime or service manager. It
  records no secret value, starts no connector, and does not treat an
  incomplete preflight as a healthy deployment. It composes the installed Flow
  connector, operator console, and repair lifecycle instead.

Options:
  --backend [web|windows|macos|linux|rdp|citrix]
                                  The execution surface that this customer
                                  deployment will use.  [default: web]
  --secret-ref TEXT               Secret reference only: env:NAME or
                                  keychain:service/item. Never pass a secret
                                  value.
  --help                          Show this message and exit.
```

### `openadapt quickstart`

```text
Usage: openadapt quickstart [OPTIONS]

  Show a task once, run it, then watch it catch a save that didn't happen.

  About 25 seconds, in a synthetic clinic app on this computer. OpenAdapt
  turns one demonstration into a program, runs it on a new note and checks the
  save in the app's database, then makes one save fail silently: the screen
  says saved, the database has nothing, and OpenAdapt stops. The program makes
  no AI calls. Nothing in the output directory is overwritten.

  With --app openemr, the same three acts run on OpenEMR 8.0.0.3 in Docker,
  with the certified referral program: referrals registered at once and
  checked in OpenEMR's record, then a referral that matches an existing chart,
  where the program stops before saving. It runs from a clone of the
  repository and needs Docker; without either it says so and exits 2.

  Other flags of the engine tutorial (for example --guided or --interactive-
  record) run that tutorial instead, unchanged.

Options:
  --out PATH               Directory for the recording, program, and run
                           reports. Default: openadapt-quickstart, suffixed
                           -2, -3, ... when taken.
  --app [mockmed|openemr]  The app to run it in. mockmed is bundled (about 22
                           seconds, no Docker). openemr runs OpenEMR 8.0.0.3
                           in Docker from a clone of the repository; the first
                           run downloads and installs it, later runs reuse it.
                           [default: mockmed]
  --headless               Hide the browser. It is shown by default when a
                           display is available.
  --no-break               Skip the last part, where one save fails silently.
  --verbose                Also print each run's engine detail and report
                           path.
  --more                   Print every next step for the last quickstart in
                           this folder (or --out) and exit. Runs nothing.
  --help                   Show this message and exit.
```

### `openadapt seal`

```text
Usage: openadapt seal [OPTIONS]

  Check an OpenAdapt Seal offline: `openadapt seal verify <file|url|folder>`.

  A folder is a run folder (or a folder of them, such as the quickstart's)
  signed on this computer; each run's report is checked against its
  `seal.json`. `openadapt seal view RUN_DIR` writes the run's Seal as one
  offline page (`RUN_DIR/seal.html`) and opens it. `openadapt seal publish
  [RUN_DIR]` uploads the run's public Seal (counts, outcomes and digests only)
  after you say yes and prints its link; `openadapt seal unpublish RUN_DIR`
  takes it down, and `openadapt seal verify <link>` checks a hosted Seal's
  signature here. Also `openadapt seal keys pin` to pin Cloud's Seal keys
  after a person confirms them. Every other argument passes to `openadapt-
  agent seal` unchanged.

Options:
  --help  Show this message and exit.
```

### `openadapt setup`

```text
Usage: openadapt setup [OPTIONS]

  Add OpenAdapt to Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Gemini CLI.

  For each one installed, register the OpenAdapt MCP server and install a
  skill that tells the agent how to turn an app task into a tool it can call
  again. By default the agent teaches read-only tasks in web apps. With --app
  and --verify it teaches saves in that one app, on the web, the desktop, or
  over RDP or Citrix. Prints every change. Running it again changes nothing
  that is already set up.

Options:
  --dry-run                       List what setup would change, and change
                                  nothing.
  --undo                          Reverse what earlier setup runs changed.
  --client [claude|cursor|codex|gemini]
                                  Set up only this client (repeat for more).
                                  Default: every one found.
  --app FILE                      deploy.yaml naming one app (web, desktop,
                                  RDP or Citrix). The agent then teaches saves
                                  in that app, each read back with --verify.
  --verify FILE                   With --app: the verify.yaml that reads the
                                  app's system of record.
  --authorization FILE            With --app: a person's signed teach
                                  authorization (openadapt-flow teach-
                                  authorization). Without one, nothing the
                                  agent teaches is admitted.
  --help                          Show this message and exit.
```

Usage: openadapt shadow [OPTIONS]

### `openadapt verify`

```text
Usage: openadapt verify [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Verify writes against the system of record, for any agent.

  Around each write your agent makes, it gets a verified receipt or a refusal,
  never an unverified success. Python agents use the SDK (`from
  openadapt.verify import ...`); any MCP client uses `openadapt verify serve`.

Options:
  --help  Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  ledger  Writes whose outcome isn't known yet, held so they aren't sent...
  serve   Serve verify_contracts, verify_begin, verify_check and...
```

### `openadapt verify ledger`

```text
Usage: openadapt verify ledger [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Writes whose outcome isn't known yet, held so they aren't sent twice.

  Every verified write goes through the ledger. A write that may have landed,
  or was refuted, is held: no worker sends it again until a read-back resolves
  it (`reconcile`) or a person checks the record (`release`). The ledger holds
  no record values.

Options:
  --help  Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  list       Show held and open writes: key, state, when it began, outcome.
  reconcile  Read held writes back and resolve the ones the store now...
  release    Release a held write after a person checked the record.
```

### `openadapt verify ledger list`

```text
Usage: openadapt verify ledger list [OPTIONS]

  Show held and open writes: key, state, when it began, outcome.

  Also each provisional CONFIRMED whose recheck is still owed, with its due
  time, so a recheck isn't lost when the server that holds it restarts.

Options:
  --ledger DIRECTORY  Ledger folder (must match the configured protected
                      journal, if set).
  --help              Show this message and exit.
```

### `openadapt verify ledger reconcile`

```text
Usage: openadapt verify ledger reconcile [OPTIONS] [KEY]

  Read held writes back and resolve the ones the store now settles.

Options:
  --contracts DIRECTORY  Folder of write contracts (<name>.yaml) the writes
                         were made under.  [required]
  --ledger DIRECTORY     Ledger folder (must match the configured protected
                         journal, if set).
  --help                 Show this message and exit.
```

### `openadapt verify ledger release`

```text
Usage: openadapt verify ledger release [OPTIONS] KEY

  Release a held write after a person checked the record.

Options:
  --by TEXT                Who checked the record.  [required]
  --reason TEXT            What they found.  [required]
  --found [absent|landed]  absent: the write isn't in the store, so it may be
                           sent again. landed: it is, so it is never sent
                           again.  [required]
  --ledger DIRECTORY       Ledger folder (must match the configured protected
                           journal, if set).
  --help                   Show this message and exit.
```

Options:

## openadapt agent

### `openadapt-agent`

```text
usage: openadapt-agent [-h] [--version] {serve,repair,authoring,example-app,emit-skill,seal} ...

Your AI agent decides what to enter. OpenAdapt enters it in the app and checks that it saved.
'serve' with no flags starts a sandbox.

positional arguments:
  {serve,repair,authoring,example-app,emit-skill,seal}
    serve               Serve workflows to your AI agent over MCP (stdio). With no flags, serve
                        the sandbox.
    repair              Control whether calling agents may help repair halted runs (local only).
    authoring           Hosted authoring mailbox client (ChatGPT.com / Claude.ai). Outbound HTTPS
                        only; not an HTTP listener.
    example-app         Run a small reports portal on this computer to teach a first task on: a
                        date-filtered sales report with an Export CSV link.
    emit-skill          Write an Agent Skill for one workflow: what it does, its inputs, and how
                        to read the result. No recorded values, step text, or secrets.
    seal                Pin OpenAdapt Cloud's Seal keys and verify a Seal offline.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --version             show program's version number and exit
```

### `openadapt-agent serve`

```text
usage: openadapt-agent serve [-h] [--mode {sandbox,attended,production}] [--bundles BUNDLES]
                             [--sandbox-engine {auto,flow,simulated}] [--authoring]
                             [--authoring-from-config] [--windows-agent-url URL]
                             [--remote-window APP] [--remote-window-title TITLE] [--citrix]
                             [--authoring-screens {off,scrubbed,unscrubbed}] [--no-ledger]
                             [--guard VERIFY_YAML] [--teach VERIFY_YAML] [--verify CONTRACTS_DIR]
                             [--verify-state VERIFY_STATE] [--teach-browser] [--contracts DIR]
                             [--sign-in NAME=ENV] [--tools-dir TOOLS_DIR] [--files-dir FILES_DIR]
                             [--teach-dir DIR] [--teach-key PEM] [--teach-policy JSON]
                             [--key-dir DIR] [--teach-authorization STATEMENT] [--teach-hold]
                             [--teach-screens {off,scrubbed,unscrubbed}] [--teach-tasks DIR]
                             [--teach-allow-origin URL] [--teach-write-adapter MODULE:ATTR]
                             [--guard-tasks DIR] [--guard-state DIR]
                             [--guard-approval {each_item,not_gated}] [--tutorial] [--allow-run]
                             [--allow-protected-export] [--allow-synthetic-recorded-defaults]
                             [--allow-attended-actions] [--url URL] [--config YAML]
                             [--policy NAME-OR-PATH] [--runs-dir RUNS_DIR] [--timeout SECONDS]
                             [--approval-mode {each_item,problems_only,not_gated}]
                             [--admissions DIR] [--approver-grant FILE]
                             [--delegate-approvals AGENT_ID] [--allow-url-override]
                             [--flow-cli FLOW_CLI] [--headed] [--allow-model-grounding]
                             [--extra-run-arg ARG] [--repair-access FILE] [--repair-dir DIR]
                             [--hold-on-halt SECONDS]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --mode {sandbox,attended,production}
                        sandbox (default with no --bundles): one synthetic workflow that shows
                        every result. production: run the compiled workflows in --bundles.
                        attended: production plus decisions on paused runs by a person at this
                        computer. --bundles without --mode stays read-only.
  --bundles BUNDLES     Bundle directory: either one compiled bundle, or a directory whose
                        immediate subdirectories are bundles. Needed for --mode production and
                        --mode attended.
  --sandbox-engine {auto,flow,simulated}
                        Advanced. flow drives the synthetic app in a hidden browser (needs the
                        tutorial extra); simulated returns the same results without opening it.
                        auto picks flow when it can.
  --authoring           Register first-demo authoring tools over local stdio: observe,
                        start_record, click, halt. Local Claude Code path is the first authoring
                        UI. Pass --url --headed to pin Playwright Chromium with empty cookies;
                        pause_for_input is how a person signs in there. --url is not the Chrome
                        window you already signed into. Omit --url to pin a unique frontmost
                        Chrome window after login (macOS; no DOM identity). Local stdio may also
                        type through the recorder; hosted MCP remains pause-only. Does not enable
                        run tools. This process stays stdio and must not be served over HTTP.
  --authoring-from-config
                        With --authoring and --config: record the app the deployment file's
                        backend: section names (windows, macos, linux, a local rdp or citrix
                        client window), the same app its runs drive. Network RDP (rdp_host) is
                        refused for authoring.
  --windows-agent-url URL
                        With --authoring: drive a native Windows app through the Flow Windows
                        agent server running on the Windows computer (for example
                        http://localhost:5001, or an SSH-forwarded port from another computer).
                        The agent's input goes through the same synthetic-input path replay uses.
                        The token comes from OAFLOW_AGENT_TOKEN.
  --remote-window APP   With --authoring: drive the RDP or Citrix session shown in this local
                        client window (app name, for example 'Microsoft Remote Desktop'). Screen-
                        only: the agent clicks pixels and presses keys.
  --remote-window-title TITLE
                        With --remote-window or --citrix: pick one window by its title.
  --citrix              With --authoring: drive the local Citrix Workspace window (--remote-window
                        overrides the app name). Screen-only.
  --authoring-screens {off,scrubbed,unscrubbed}
                        With --authoring: let the agent see the pinned window through the screen
                        tool, so it can drive a native Windows app or a remote session from
                        pixels. scrubbed removes identifiers first and shares nothing if that
                        fails. Default off.
  --no-ledger           Don't serve the task-ledger tools (open_job, get_job, add_items,
                        record_evidence, ask_user, get_answer, change_constraint, close_job). They
                        are on whenever runs or guarded saves are.
  --guard VERIFY_YAML   Serve only the guarded-save tools (guard_begin, guard_commit,
                        guard_confirm) for any agent's own writes. VERIFY_YAML is the verify-run
                        file: the system-of-record reader and the record the save must produce.
                        Needs --guard-tasks and --guard-state.
  --teach VERIFY_YAML   Add the teach tools: the agent does a task once in the app at --url (or
                        the --config backend: Windows, macOS, Linux, RDP, Citrix), Flow checks the
                        saved record through VERIFY_YAML's verifier, compiles the run, and once it
                        is admitted the agent calls it as a tool with no model calls. Run 1 makes
                        a real entry: use a test copy.
  --verify CONTRACTS_DIR
                        Serve only the verify tools (verify_contracts, verify_begin, verify_check,
                        verify_recheck): any agent calls them around its own writes, and gets a
                        verified receipt or a refusal. CONTRACTS_DIR holds the write contracts
                        (<name>.yaml, openadapt.verify/v1).
  --verify-state VERIFY_STATE
                        With --verify: where baselines and receipts go (default
                        ~/.openadapt/verify)
  --teach-browser       Serve the read-only teach tools: the agent does a browser task once at a
                        URL the person gives, the task ends in a download, and it becomes a
                        taught_<name> tool that runs with no model calls. The browser sends no
                        POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE. Read-only teaching needs that guard, so a
                        --config naming a desktop, RDP or Citrix app is refused; teach those apps
                        with --teach VERIFY_YAML --config, where every save is read back. A web
                        --config is refused too: --teach-browser takes its URL from the person.
  --contracts DIR       With --teach-browser: folder of write contracts (<name>.yaml,
                        openadapt.verify/v1). A taught task that names one may save, and every run
                        of it is verified against it.
  --sign-in NAME=ENV    With --teach-browser: an input the server types for the agent, from
                        environment variable ENV (a username or password). The value never reaches
                        the agent or the taught program. Repeat for more.
  --tools-dir TOOLS_DIR
                        With --teach-browser: where taught tools live (default ~/.openadapt/tools)
  --files-dir FILES_DIR
                        With --teach-browser: where downloaded files go (default
                        ~/Downloads/OpenAdapt)
  --teach-dir DIR       With --teach: where drafts and taught programs live (default
                        RUNS_DIR/teach)
  --teach-key PEM       With --teach and --teach-policy: the encrypted key of the registered agent
                        that may admit what it taught (passphrase from
                        $OPENADAPT_JIT_KEY_PASSPHRASE). Without it, a person admits at a terminal
                        (openadapt-flow compile-agent admit).
  --teach-policy JSON   With --teach-key: the admission policy a person signed (openadapt-flow jit
                        sign-policy). The agent admits its own draft only if it sets
                        allow_self_admission.
  --key-dir DIR         With --teach: the JIT key directory (default $OPENADAPT_JIT_KEY_DIR or
                        ~/.openadapt/jit)
  --teach-authorization STATEMENT
                        With --teach or --teach-browser: a person's signed teach authorization
                        (openadapt-flow teach-authorization). Run 1 is scoped by it; without one,
                        --teach drafts are refused at admission and --teach-browser teaches and
                        runs no write. With --repair-access: it lets a calling agent's fix be
                        approved (it must cover repair). Its signer is checked under the
                        deployment config's approvers section (--config) only.
  --teach-hold          With --teach on a web app: a person also approves every save in the
                        client's form (always on for other surfaces).
  --teach-screens {off,scrubbed,unscrubbed}
                        With --teach: add teach_screen so the agent sees the app (RDP and Citrix
                        need it). scrubbed shares nothing if scrubbing fails.
  --teach-tasks DIR     With --teach: folder of <task_id>.json task files the operator wrote
                        (openadapt.guard-task/v1). teach_start must then name one, and its record
                        and inputs come from the file, not the agent.
  --teach-allow-origin URL
                        With --teach: another origin run 1's browser may reach (a sign-in host, a
                        CDN); every origin but the app's is refused otherwise
  --teach-write-adapter MODULE:ATTR
                        With --teach: the app's write adapter, so run 1's writes are read before
                        they are sent (openadapt_flow.teach_scope.WriteAdapter)
  --guard-tasks DIR     With --guard: folder of <task_id>.json task files the operator wrote
  --guard-state DIR     With --guard: folder for baselines, approval requests, receipts and the
                        per-task ledger
  --guard-approval {each_item,not_gated}
                        With --guard: each_item (default) holds every save for a person
  --tutorial            Older name for --mode sandbox. Synthetic only. Cannot be combined with
                        --bundles, --url, or --config.
  --allow-run           Older name for --mode production (with --bundles) or --mode sandbox
                        (without). Without a mode or this flag, --bundles stays read-only.
  --allow-protected-export
                        DANGER: export raw workflow labels, recorded values, intents, local paths,
                        reports, stdout, stderr, and exception detail to the MCP client. Off by
                        default; enable only for an explicitly trusted local client inside the
                        protected data boundary.
  --allow-synthetic-recorded-defaults
                        DEMO ONLY: let omitted workflow parameters reuse recorded values. Use only
                        with synthetic demonstrations; production requires every declared
                        parameter so a run cannot silently target the recorded customer or record.
  --allow-attended-actions
                        Part of --mode attended. Register governed Reject/Teach/Escalate tools for
                        signed durable pauses. With --config, also register Continue/Skip through
                        Flow's deployment-bound live verifier and deterministic resume path.
  --url URL             Target app URL passed to every `openadapt-flow run` (operator-fixed)
  --config YAML         Deployment config YAML forwarded to `openadapt-flow run --config`. With
                        --authoring-from-config, its backend: section also names the app to
                        record.
  --policy NAME-OR-PATH
                        Certifying policy forwarded to `openadapt-flow run --policy` and used by
                        get_workflow's certification check
  --runs-dir RUNS_DIR   Directory for run records and evidence (default:
                        $OPENADAPT_AGENT_RUNS_DIR, else ~/.openadapt/runs; the sandbox uses
                        ~/.openadapt/agent-sandbox). Never relative to the folder the client
                        starts the server in.
  --timeout SECONDS     Per-call timeout for each governed run (default: 600)
  --approval-mode {each_item,problems_only,not_gated}
                        Per-save approval passed to every `openadapt-flow run`. Unset (the
                        default): Flow decides, and each save waits for approval (each_item) under
                        every profile; a run waiting for that approval reports needs_review.
                        not_gated turns the pause off for every run this server starts, and each
                        run's result and Flow's report record that. Callers can't change it.
  --admissions DIR      Add prepare_admission, list_admissions and decide_admission: the
                        `openadapt-flow admit` command over recordings in DIR/recordings and
                        shadow candidates in DIR/shadow-candidates. A person decides in the
                        client's form, or, with --delegate-approvals, the agent decides as that
                        approver. An agent can't decide an admission it prepared.
  --approver-grant FILE
                        With --admissions and --delegate-approvals: the approver grant a person
                        signed (openadapt-flow approver-grant sign) that lets AGENT_ID decide
                        admissions. It must name AGENT_ID, cover the workflow and let an agent
                        approve saves; Flow verifies it on every decision. Without it only a
                        person decides.
  --delegate-approvals AGENT_ID
                        Let the calling agent answer saves that wait for an approval, as the
                        opaque id AGENT_ID (for example agent:intake-bot). Adds the
                        list_approval_requests and answer_approval_request tools. Flow accepts the
                        agent's answer only under a person-signed approver grant (openadapt-flow
                        run --approver-policy) that names AGENT_ID and allows an agent for that
                        step; by default only a person may answer. Runs this server starts record
                        AGENT_ID as their initiator, so the agent can never approve its own runs.
                        Flow records the agent and the grant's digest as the approver.
  --allow-url-override  Permit MCP callers to pass a per-call `url` argument (default: the target
                        URL is fixed by --url/--config at server start)
  --flow-cli FLOW_CLI   Command used to invoke the flow CLI (default: this interpreter's `python
                        -m openadapt_flow`, so the flow installed alongside this server is always
                        the one that runs); may contain spaces, e.g. 'openadapt-flow'
  --headed              Keep a deployment-configured attended web session visible to the local
                        operator (required for web Continue/Skip).
  --allow-model-grounding
                        Explicit CLI opt-in for configured off-box model grounding. A deployment
                        config may also opt in; otherwise verification remains local.
  --extra-run-arg ARG   Extra argument appended to every `openadapt-flow run` invocation
                        (repeatable; operator-fixed, e.g. --extra-run-arg=--allow-unencrypted for
                        a demo bundle)
  --repair-access FILE  Screen access setting for repairs, written by `openadapt-agent repair
                        access`. Without it, halted runs still return needs_repair but no screens,
                        and teach_repair is not offered.
  --repair-dir DIR      Where repair tokens, approvals, and candidates live (default
                        RUNS_DIR/.repair).
  --hold-on-halt SECONDS
                        With --repair-access, keep a halted browser run's page open this long so
                        teach_repair acts on it (default 300; 0 turns it off).
```

### `openadapt-agent repair`

```text
usage: openadapt-agent repair [-h] {access,approve-screen} ...

positional arguments:
  {access,approve-screen}
    access              Set screen access for repairs for one workflow or the whole organization.
    approve-screen      Look at the exact screen a calling agent would get for one repair, and
                        approve it.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
```

### `openadapt-agent repair access`

```text
usage: openadapt-agent repair access [-h] (--workflow WORKFLOW | --org) --screens
                                     {off,scrubbed_only,ask_each_time,allow_unscrubbed} --by BY
                                     --file FILE

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --workflow WORKFLOW   Workflow name from list_workflows
  --org                 Default for every workflow
  --screens {off,scrubbed_only,ask_each_time,allow_unscrubbed}
  --by BY               Your name, recorded with the setting
  --file FILE           The --repair-access file
```

### `openadapt-agent repair approve-screen`

```text
usage: openadapt-agent repair approve-screen [-h] --by BY --repair-access FILE --repair-dir DIR
                                             token_id

positional arguments:
  token_id              token_id from the needs_repair result

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --by BY               Your name, recorded with the approval
  --repair-access FILE
  --repair-dir DIR
```

### `openadapt-agent authoring`

```text
usage: openadapt-agent authoring [-h] {connect} ...

positional arguments:
  {connect}
    connect   Claim an openadapt://runner link or pack URL, poll wait=0, and prompt Allow per chat
              account

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

### `openadapt-agent authoring connect`

```text
usage: openadapt-agent authoring connect [-h] [--url URL] [--headed] target

Claim an openadapt://runner link or pack URL, poll wait=0, and prompt Allow per chat account.
Overlay chrome stays Desktop-only. Continue uses record_observed; it does not type secrets. This
process only makes outbound HTTPS.

positional arguments:
  target      openadapt://runner?pack=…&bind=oab_…&origin=https://openadapt.ai or
              https://openadapt.ai/j/{id} (bind required to claim)

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --url URL   Launch Playwright Chromium with empty cookies at this URL. Not the browser you are
              already signed into.
  --headed    Keep the Playwright window visible (required to sign in in the app).
```

### `openadapt-agent seal`

```text
usage: openadapt-agent seal [-h] {verify,keys} ...

positional arguments:
  {verify,keys}
    verify       Check a Seal (receipt, run report, or webhook JSON).
    keys         Pin or show the Cloud Seal keys this computer trusts.

options:
  -h, --help     show this help message and exit
```

### `openadapt-agent seal verify`

```text
usage: openadapt-agent seal verify [-h] [--keys KEYS] [--json] target

positional arguments:
  target       Path, https:// URL, or - for stdin

options:
  -h, --help   show this help message and exit
  --keys KEYS  Pinned key file (default: your pinned keys)
  --json       Print the verdict as JSON
```

### `openadapt-agent seal keys`

```text
usage: openadapt-agent seal keys [-h] {pin,show} ...

positional arguments:
  {pin,show}
    pin       Fetch /api/public/seal-keys and pin new keys after a person confirms each one.
    show      List pinned keys with fingerprints.

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
```

### `openadapt-agent seal keys pin`

```text
usage: openadapt-agent seal keys pin [-h] [--url URL] [--path PATH] [--confirm KEY_ID]

options:
  -h, --help        show this help message and exit
  --url URL         Key registry URL (default https://app.openadapt.ai/api/public/seal-keys)
  --path PATH       Pinned key file (default ~/.openadapt/seal-keys.json)
  --confirm KEY_ID  Trust this key id without a prompt, after checking its fingerprint out of
                    band. Repeatable.
```

### `openadapt-agent seal keys show`

```text
usage: openadapt-agent seal keys show [-h] [--path PATH]

options:
  -h, --help   show this help message and exit
  --path PATH
```
